narrative.overview: JobCrush happens in a dark, quiet room. The interface is the room — matte charcoal surfaces, thin lines, muted greys — and it stays deliberately self-effacing, because the one thing that matters in the room is the CV: a warm, cream, serif sheet of paper that reads like a real printed page. Gold is lamplight: it falls only on what is on the page right now, or on the moment something the person said becomes part of their record. When something glows on this screen, it earned it. This identity was not invented; it is the shipped product's own register, chosen again by the owner on 2026-08-08 against three deliberately louder alternative worlds.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds: the dark room (the game — confirm deck, question game, job decks, tailoring, profile) and a warm light register (import, sign-in, settings, admin); the paper is a third material living in both. Sign-up enters the dark room at Confirm and stays there through the question game — no register change between those back-to-back screens
One accent — gold is rationed and semantic, never decorative
Quiet chrome: 1px lines, tonal layering, muted text; the content is the show
The machine speaks in the first person, in short plain words (observed practice, not locked)

rules.name: The Gold Law
rules.body: Gold marks what is on the rendered CV right now, or the moment a fact joins the record. Grey (Reserve) marks what is saved for later. Gold never decorates; one glowing thing per screen is the ceiling.

rules.name: The Two Rooms Rule
rules.body: A surface commits to one register — dark room or light register — and uses the paper palette only for things that are literally the printed page.

rules.name: The Serif Means Her Rule
rules.body: Serif text is reserved for the person's own document and sentences quoted from it. The machine never speaks in the serif.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest; depth is tonal. If something casts a shadow, the person should be able to imagine picking it up.

rules.name: The Fit-Width Paper Rule
rules.body: The CV paper renders at true page proportions (640×905) and is scaled to fit via transform — never reflowed.

rules.name: The Still List Rule
rules.body: A list never reorders itself under the person as they work through it. A row changes its appearance, never its position.

dos: Do keep gold semantic (Gold Law): on-the-page, the reward beat, the one primary action — and nothing else.
Do switch to the serif whenever the person's own document or sentences appear.
Do reuse the shipped motion values (720ms chip flight, 460ms bump, 340ms deal-in, 8px drag activation / 90px commit) instead of re-timing per screen.
Do state costs in plain words at the moment of a change, in the machine's first-person voice.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion on every animation, and keep muted-on-raised text at the AA-checked #8a95a2.
donts: Don't put a shadow on a surface that isn't a physical object (paper, flying card, phone frame).
Don't mix the dark room and the light register on one surface, or use pure white for anything that represents the page (paper is #f6f2ea).
Don't reorder a list under the person, ever (Still List Rule).
Don't add a second accent colour to the dark room — gold is alone by design.
Don't show designer instrumentation (counters, budgets, internal vocabulary) on the person's screen — prototype chrome only.
